Robotics deployment is now front and center. Last week, we at Savant co-hosted "deploying physical AI in the real world" with Instawork and we broke a new record.  

In one week, we drew over 700+ registrations!  

Incredible to have Gary Kagan (Instawork), Rishabh Jangir (Skild AI) , Arjun Dhawan (Dexterity, Inc.), Kaan Dogrusoz (Weave Robotics) share their deployment insights.  

A few notes: 
-Diversity of data beats volume. Every panelist ranked it above raw hours logged. 

- Deployment is the real data engine: once robots are live, teleoperation fallbacks and autonomous fleet interventions become more valuable than anything collected in a lab, and the teams winning are the ones treating deployment itself as the flywheel 

- Vertical vs. horizontal: going deep on one embodiment gets you tighter feedback loops and faster iteration, while building across embodiments trades that for generalization — and it fundamentally changes what data strategy even means for your team  

Thanks Instawork & Nebius for supporting the event! For those who missed, we will be sharing the recording soon!

Shoutout to April Liu & Amanda Pires for making the planning of the event a smooth one.

🚚 The Warehouse Job Nobody Wants, and a Robot Race to Replace It
Ask anyone who's worked a loading dock what the worst job in the building is, and you'll get the same answer: unloading trucks. Boxes shift in transit, stack unevenly, come in every size and weight, and someone has to physically pull each one out, hour after hour, shift after shift. It's exhausting, it's injury-prone, and it's one of the last truly manual jobs left in modern logistics.

That's exactly why two of robotics' biggest names are racing to solve it, from opposite directions.

📦 Boston Dynamics' Stretch: unload-first
Single vacuum-gripper arm, purpose-built for speed. Years of proven, multi-site deployment with DHL, Gap, H&M. Loading is on the roadmap, not yet shipped.

🤖 Dexterity's Mech: load-first
Dual arms with force and touch sensing, more dexterous by design. Dexterity already solved unloading with its earlier robot, DexR, then picked loading as the harder problem to tackle next. That's exactly why FedEx chose it for Hagerstown.

🟦 Fox Robotics: a different lane entirely
Austin-based, palletized freight only, retrofit autonomous forklifts. Needs volume, generally 8+ dock doors, to beat a human driver on cost per pallet.

🎯 Why this matters:
Only 4% of supply chain leaders have deployed these robots even at pilot scale. That's a business case problem, not a technology one. Today's deployments are high school science projects, early movers testing before the ROI is proven. But the gap is closing fast. When the business case clears, expect a rush, not a ramp.

🔑 The real opportunity:
3PLs run floor-loaded, palletized, and parcel freight through the same docks in the same week. Whoever closes the loop, one robot, every freight type, won't just have a product. They'll have a moat.

Who's going to win the robot race?

Warehouse robots have traditionally performed best with predictable, repeatable work. Truck loading rarely follows a set pattern.

Boxes come in different sizes, shapes, and weights. Some are damaged, while others have labels telling workers which side must stay up.

Dexterity, Inc. is using #physicalAI to take on that changing environment with its Mech "superhumanoid" robot, while Beckhoff Automation USA worked with the company on the controls connecting motion, safety, navigation, and data.

I spoke with Dexterity’s Robert Sun and Beckhoff Automation's Doug Schuchart about the technology behind Mech and what it takes to automate a task with so many variables.

“It’s just like you’re playing Tetris,” said Sun. “This is a weird game that you have to play or learn on the job that can’t really be automated, no matter how hard you think about it.”

We also talked about Dexterity’s origins, its work with Beckhoff and #EtherCAT, how that relationship evolved, and even anime. 👀

Truck loading is the uber-gauntlet for Physical AI. It looks like a manipulation problem, but it is actually an incredibly complex long-horizon reasoning and prediction problem!  Every package changes the future of a truck load. A placement that works now can create instability, waste space, or block the next move. 

If prediction gets you to the dock door, production gets you to scale.

Production is hard. Very hard. Customer operations are demanding, and operational KPIs are non-negotiable. Price-perfomance drives the business case and hype bites the dust!

Today, Dexterity, Inc. and FedEx are glad to share that the first Physical AI world model, Foresight, and the first superhumanoid robot, Mech, have delivered on both fronts. FedEx will deploy the first enterprise-grade, safe, superhuman, AI-powered mixed-box truck loading system at commercial scale!

Grateful to Raj Subramaniam, Kawal Preet, Vinay D'Souza, O.P. Skaaksrud, Stephanie C., Steven Schwartzberg and the teams at FedEx and Dexterity who made this possible.

The announcement of FedEx and Dexterity, Inc. expanding robotics trailer loading to the Hagerstown Hub is an exciting milestone—and one I’m incredibly proud because enterprise-scale deployment of Physical AI is fundamentally different from scaling digital AI.

While software can often be deployed with the push of a button, Physical AI must reliably operate in the real world, where every decision interacts with people, equipment, facilities, and constantly changing environments. Getting from an impressive demo to production at enterprise scale requires years of disciplined engineering and operational excellence.

True production readiness demands capabilities well beyond AI models:

* Product & Functional Safety
* Validation & Verification
* Component Selection & Qualification
* Reliability Growth Modeling & Testing
* Supply Chain Development & Execution
* Inbound & Outbound Logistics Integration
* Manufacturing Planning & Certification
* Parts, Service & Maintenance Readiness
* Operator Training & Site Readiness

This is why scaling Physical AI is so challenging—and why so few companies have successfully crossed the gap from lab demonstrations to sustained production deployments.

Congratulations to Samir Menon and the entire Dexterity team, and to Stephanie C. and FedEx team, on this achievement. This milestone reflects years of collaboration, relentless innovation, rigorous testing, and a shared commitment to operational excellence.

I’m excited to see what comes next as Physical AI continues its journey from promising technology to enterprise-scale reality.

Robert Sun Mukesh R. Steven Schwartzberg
